title: Preserving metadata with functools.wraps

kcs.statement: Without functools.wraps, the decorated name's __name__ and __doc__ are those of the wrapper, not of the original function.
Applying @functools.wraps(func) to the wrapper copies __module__, __name__, __qualname__, __doc__ and __annotations__ from func and merges func's __dict__ into the wrapper's.
functools.wraps sets wrapper.__wrapped__ to func, so inspect.signature reports the original signature and the undecorated function stays reachable.

problem_ideas: Predict help(f) output for a decorated function with and without wraps
Add wraps to a @log_calls decorator and check __name__ and __doc__
Call f.__wrapped__ to bypass a slow decorator in a test
Compare inspect.signature(f) before and after adding wraps
Explain why two decorated functions both show up as 'wrapper' in a stack trace
Write a decorator that copies metadata by hand, then replace it with wraps
